items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Sidney asked if I'd go in with him with a quartet, the wonderful Kenny Kersey on piano and Vic Dickenson on trombone, and myself.

ctx.x: Sidney Bechet was very strict with drummers, he had that reputation, I'd heard that from Zutty, and the time had to go exactly his way. He was rather gruff and rather hard to get close to. But once Kenny Kersey and I got the feel of the thing, he seemed pleased and I never had any serious words with him. He seemed very pleased with what we did for him. There was a Bechet album issued in France the last few years -- 2 or 3 years ago, and it's a long playing album, three playing sides, three long playing records, I…

and I find it very hard, I'm trying to find out, I'm looking at the album now, it says 'recorded in the Rendezvous Club during his visit to the states" in '49 or '50. And he lived in France then and he visited here. The band was Vic Dickson, Kenny Kersey and myself, and the Rendezvous Club, it says here on the album, they recorded a whole night of music in Philadelphia in that club.

Wow. That must have been something for you guys to be playing with the great Sidney Bechet. I've got to find that album, Cliff, and have you loan it to me so I can make some tapes from it. Because that should be a masterpiece.
